stories.headline: Anthropic signs 12+ data center lease LOIs covering 1+ GW, seeks Google financial guarantee

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has signed more than a dozen preliminary agreements to lease US data centers with combined capacity exceeding 1 gigawatt.
Anthropic executives discussed having Google provide a financial guarantee on the lease payments, building on Google's role co-designing the server chips Anthropic would use.
Google declined to comment on the discussions and Anthropic did not immediately respond.
Apollo Global Management and Blackstone are providing private credit as part of the wider financing structure tied to Anthropic compute.
Anthropic raised $65 billion in late May at a $965 billion post-money valuation and filed confidentially for a US IPO earlier this month.
Google had earlier announced plans to invest up to $40 billion in Anthropic.

stories.headline: Bezos' Prometheus raises $12B Series B at $41B valuation for 'artificial general engineer'

key_facts.fact: Prometheus, the physical AI startup co-founded by Jeff Bezos and Vik Bajaj, announced a $12B Series B at a $41B valuation.
Investors include JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, DST Global and Arch Venture Partners; Bezos contributed again after being the largest backer of the $6.2B Series A.
Prometheus launched in November 2025 with $6.2B in seed funding; total funding now exceeds $18B in less than a year.
Prometheus is building what Bezos calls an 'artificial general engineer' — AI tools to compress the design-to-manufacturing cycle for physical products from years to months.
The company employs about 150 people across San Francisco, London and Zurich and has not disclosed any commercial revenue.

A large portion of the capital will go toward compute, with Bezos saying the work is 'very compute intensive,' especially for data generation; the startup has poached employees from OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Nvidia.

stories.headline: Crusoe pushed out of 1.8GW Wyoming AI data center after Google raised cost and timing concerns

key_facts.fact: Crusoe paused work on Project Jade, a 1.8GW data center campus planned in Cheyenne, Wyoming, that was designed to scale up to 10GW.
Bloomberg reported that Google raised concerns about costs and the construction timetable under Crusoe's management, leading the company to leave the project.
Crusoe said it has contracted 4.9GW of data center infrastructure for Crusoe Cloud outside Wyoming, with a total pipeline exceeding 40GW.
Crusoe is valued at $10 billion and counts Nvidia, Salesforce and Mubadala Capital among its backers.

Tallgrass, Crusoe's energy partner on Project Jade and backed by Blackstone, confirmed Crusoe demobilized from the site months ago and is in talks with other AI infrastructure companies to replace it.

Crusoe's flagship Abilene, Texas campus has had reliability issues, with buildings going offline for days due to winter weather affecting liquid cooling, and Oracle and OpenAI declined to lease additional capacity there.

stories.headline: EngineAI files confidentially for Hong Kong IPO at $1.5B valuation amid China robotics rush

key_facts.fact: Shenzhen-based humanoid robotics startup EngineAI has filed confidentially for an initial public offering in Hong Kong.
EngineAI is working with China International Capital Corp (CICC) and CITIC Securities on the proposed listing, with size and timing still undetermined.
EngineAI was valued at more than $1.5 billion after a 200 million yuan ($27.9 million) Series B in April, led by Henan CICC Huirong Fund Management and Luxshare-ICT.
Founded in 2023, EngineAI gained attention last year for a video of its humanoid robot performing a front flip.
EngineAI joins a pipeline of Chinese robotics IPO candidates including Unitree Robotics and robotic-hand maker PaXini Tech.

stories.headline: Genspark raises $100M Series B extension at $2.6B valuation, up 63% in three months

key_facts.fact: Agentic workplace startup Genspark raised $100 million in Series B extension funding at a $2.6 billion post-money valuation.
The valuation marks a 63% jump in just three months and brings Genspark's total funding to more than $645 million.
Return investors in the round were Sozo Ventures, UpHonest Capital and South Korea's Mirae Asset.
Genspark's previous Series B extension in early April 2026 brought the round to $385 million at a $1.6 billion valuation.
Genspark, led by CEO Eric Jing, orchestrates more than 70 AI models and sells an 'AI employee' product (Genspark Claw) for research, scheduling, communication and code deployment.

stories.headline: Google taps Samsung for Icefish TPU memory I/O die as TSMC capacity tightens

key_facts.fact: Google is in talks to outsource production of the memory input/output die for its 10th-generation TPU, codenamed Icefish, to Samsung's 2-nanometer foundry process.
TSMC will continue to manufacture the TPU's core computing engine, expected to use its 1.4-nanometer process.
The split-foundry strategy reflects TSMC's saturated capacity for AI chips and Google's desire to lock in Samsung HBM supply.
Samsung has supplied more than 60% of the HBM used in Google's TPUs over the past year.
Icefish is expected to enter mass production as early as 2028, with discussions still in early stages.
Google is also reportedly in talks with Intel for some TPU components, in addition to Samsung.

stories.headline: J&J's IMAAVY shows durable hemoglobin response in pivotal wAIHA trial at EHA Congress

key_facts.fact: Johnson & Johnson on June 11 presented the first comprehensive Phase 2/3 ENERGY results at the EHA 2026 Congress in Stockholm showing IMAAVY (nipocalimab-aahu) produced a statistically significant durable hemoglobin response in warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (wAIHA)

In the 30 mg/kg arm, mean hemoglobin improved by at least 1 g/dL as early as Week 1; about three times as many patients achieved durable Hgb levels versus placebo by Week 24, and nearly two-thirds hit both ≥10 g/dL and ≥2 g/dL increase targets

Warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (wAIHA) is a rare, life-threatening autoantibody-driven condition with no FDA-approved treatment; the data support a supplemental BLA that the FDA granted Priority Review in Q2 2026
IMAAVY is designed to target pathogenic IgG autoantibodies that destroy red blood cells in wAIHA while preserving broader immune function; the abstract (S300) was presented June 11, 16:45-18:00 CEST

stories.headline: KKR launches Helix Digital Infrastructure with $10B+ from Kuwait, Nvidia and Vistra

key_facts.fact: KKR, the Kuwait Investment Authority, Nvidia and Vistra launched Helix Digital Infrastructure with more than $10 billion of committed capital to build AI data centers, power and connectivity.
Helix will be led by former AWS chief Adam Selipsky, with KKR's global head of digital infrastructure Waldemar Szlezak as chief investment officer.
Nvidia will be a cornerstone strategic partner, supplying its DSX AI-factory architecture; Vistra will be Helix's preferred power provider.
Helix sits inside KKR's infrastructure business, which manages more than $100 billion globally and has invested over $70 billion in digital infrastructure and power.
The launch follows Apollo and Blackstone's recently announced $35 billion private credit program linked to Anthropic projects.

stories.headline: Nvidia pitches Vera CPUs to Chinese customers with orders open and August availability

key_facts.fact: Nvidia told Chinese clients its Vera CPU for AI data centers could be available as soon as August and that they can begin placing orders.
One major Chinese cloud provider is preparing an initial order of more than 300 dual-Vera-CPU servers, planned for testing in overseas data centers first.
Nvidia is targeting roughly $20 billion in Vera revenue by the end of its fiscal year to end-January, with single-CPU prices well north of $20,000.
Vera is Nvidia's first standalone CPU, designed for agentic AI, and positions the Arm-based chip against Intel and AMD in the server CPU market.
The pitch comes after Nvidia's market share in China effectively dropped to zero amid US export controls on advanced AI chips.

stories.headline: OpenAI to acquire Ona to give Codex secure cloud environments for long-running agents

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced an agreement to acquire Ona, a cloud execution and orchestration startup, to extend Codex with secure, persistent environments for AI agents.
Ona's customer-controlled execution model lets agents operate inside an organization's own cloud while OpenAI provides intelligence and orchestration.
Codex now supports more than 5 million weekly active users, up from 3 million in April, and the deal aims to let Codex handle longer multi-step tasks.
Knowledge workers now make up roughly one in five Codex users and are growing at more than triple the rate of the core developer group.
Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed; the acquisition is subject to customary closing and regulatory approvals, after which Ona's team will join the Codex group.
Ona had previously supported around 2 million developers with cloud-based development environments.

stories.headline: FDA grants Priority Review to Roche's Tecentriq combo for stage III dMMR colon cancer

key_facts.fact: On June 11 Roche said the FDA accepted its sBLA for adjuvant Tecentriq (atezolizumab) and Tecentriq Hybreza plus FOLFOX6 chemotherapy in stage III deficient DNA mismatch repair (dMMR)/MSI-H colon cancer, granting Priority Review with a decision expected by October 9, 2026

Filing rests on the Phase 3 ATOMIC study (712 patients), recently published in The New England Journal of Medicine, showing the Tecentriq-FOLFOX6 combination reduced the risk of disease recurrence or death by 50% vs chemotherapy alone
36-month disease-free survival was 86% in the Tecentriq+FOLFOX6 arm versus 76% with FOLFOX6 alone; safety was consistent with previous Tecentriq studies

Separately on June 11, Guardant Health said the FDA approved Guardant360 CDx as a companion diagnostic for Boehringer Ingelheim's Hernexeos (zongertinib), the first targeted therapy for HER2-mutant advanced non-small cell lung cancer

stories.headline: SpaceX prices largest-ever IPO at $135/share, raising $75B at $1.77T valuation

key_facts.fact: SpaceX priced its IPO at $135 per share on June 11, selling 555.6 million shares to raise about $75 billion, the biggest-ever U.S. IPO and topping Saudi Aramco's $25.6B 2019 deal
The $135 price implies a fully diluted valuation of about $1.77 trillion, making SpaceX the seventh-largest publicly traded U.S. company and worth more than Tesla (~$1.6T)
Musk keeps 82.4% of voting power through 5.22 billion Class B shares; underwriters have an option for 83.33M more shares ($11.2B) within 30 days
SpaceX targeted retail investors for ~30% of the offering — about $22.5 billion — versus a typical 5%-10%; the IPO was more than four times oversubscribed
SpaceX generated about $18.7B in revenue in 2025 but posted an operating loss of $4.2B; it begins trading June 12 on Nasdaq under ticker SPCX
Lead underwriters are Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, Citigroup and JPMorgan Chase, with 18 other banks participating

stories.headline: Barcelona's Theker raises $85M Series A from CRV, Samsung and LVMH for AI factory robots

key_facts.fact: Barcelona-based AI robotics company Theker raised $85 million (€73M) in a Series A led by CRV.
The round marks Samsung's first-ever investment in a Spanish company, LVMH's first bet on the Spanish startup ecosystem, and one of CRV's first investments in Spain.
Other participants include Cathay Innovation, 20VC, Henkel Ventures, Korelya, Bright Pixel Capital (Sonae), and existing investors Inditex, Kfund and Kibo Ventures.
Theker calls its round the largest robotics Series A ever raised in Europe.

Founded in 2022 by Carla Gómez Cano and Jiaqiang Ye Zhu, Theker builds AI-native generalist robots that adapt in real time to mixed SKUs, irregular shapes and operational variability without manual reprogramming.
Theker is already deploying its robots in industrial settings — for example, working with Inditex to automate tasks in the retailer's logistics operations.

stories.headline: Trump cancels Iran strikes after two-day exchange, claims imminent deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: On June 11, Trump posted on Truth Social that he had cancelled scheduled U.S. strikes on Iran after discussions reached 'the highest level of Iranian leadership' and were approved

Trump's reversal came hours after he warned the U.S. would hit Iran 'VERY HARD TONIGHT' and threatened to take 'total control' of Iran's oil and gas industries, including the Kharg Island oil terminal

Trump said the draft framework would extend the ceasefire, reopen the Strait of Hormuz and launch 60 days of negotiations on Iran's nuclear program, with a signing potentially in Europe over the weekend led by VP Vance

The pivot followed two consecutive days of strikes: the U.S. fired 49 Tomahawk missiles at targets near Tehran while Iran's IRGC launched 12 ballistic missiles at Jordan's Al-Azraq/Muwaffaq Salti air base and claimed strikes on 18 U.S. targets in Kuwait and Bahrain

Iran's foreign ministry tempered Trump's claim, saying 'so far, Iran has not reached a final conclusion on the agreement'; semi-official Tasnim noted Trump had publicly declared a deal imminent 38 times in the prior two months
Trump said the U.S. naval blockade would 'remain in full force and effect until this Transaction is finalized' and that Iran would agree never to have a nuclear weapon

stories.headline: Ukraine downs 102 of 117 Russian drones overnight as Shahed attacks continue

key_facts.fact: On the night of June 11-12, Russia attacked Ukraine with 117 Shahed-type, Gerbera, Italmas and Parodiya decoy strike UAVs, launched from Orel, Kursk, Millerovo and occupied Crimea
Ukrainian air defense neutralized 102 of the 117 drones; 14 strike UAVs hit seven locations and debris fell at eight more, with several enemy UAVs still in airspace as of 08:00
Ukrainian commander Oleksandr Syrskyi said on June 11 that Ukrainian FPV drones now outnumber Russian FPVs on the battlefield by an unspecified ratio that 'is growing'
The June 11-12 barrage follows a larger attack the previous night (June 10-11) when Russia launched 221 drones plus two Iskander-M ballistic missiles and Ukraine downed 195

organizations: Institute for the Study of War

stories.headline: Xiaomi open-sources MiMo Code V0.1.0, claims edge over Claude Code on long-horizon tasks

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi's MiMo AI team open-sourced MiMo Code V0.1.0, a terminal-native AI coding assistant, claiming it outperforms Anthropic's Claude Code on agentic coding benchmarks.
Running the same MiMo-V2.5-Pro model in both harnesses, MiMo Code scored 62% on SWE-Bench Pro versus 57% for Claude Code, and 73% on Terminal Bench 2 versus 68% for Claude Code.

In a double-blind A/B evaluation with 576 developers across 474 private repositories, MiMo Code's win rate rose above 65% past 200 execution steps, while the two systems split roughly 50/50 under 200 steps.
MiMo Code is a fork of the open-source OpenCode project, released under the MIT license, and ships with free access to MiMo V2.5 with a 1-million-token context window.
MiMo Code supports importing existing Claude Code configurations in one step and connecting to providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM.
The GitHub repository was created on June 10, 2026 and tagged its v0.1.0 release the same day.
